doc.title: George Wein — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Water and phone break; how he remembers the stories in his book
summary: A brief pause, then Wein says he told only the stories he remembers vividly.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Wow. Okay. Do you need any water or anything? You okay?
I'm all right for the moment. [Phone rings, Levy asked Kimery if phone sound is interfering with recording.]
Are you getting what you want?
Yes! Yes. And you're right on script, having not read it.
You're right on my script even though you didn't read it. So we're perfectly in sync here.

The story of what I know … and so many people ask me, "How do you do it? … I don't remember everything about my life, but what I do remember, I remember vividly. So those are the stories that I told. I didn't try to dig up stories that I didn't remember. If I remembered it vividly, I put it in the book. If I didn't … I mean, people are always telling me, "Well didn't you remember this?" Just like you told me about John's program. I don't remember the details of that program.
